title: The parable's allegory: landowner, vineyard, laborers, and the hours
english: "The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard" (Matthew 20:1). You have heard, beloved, the Lord's parable from the Gospel; now hear the interpretation that we will offer as best we can. The landowner of the great house—that is, the master God. For the house is the world, and its master is the God who created it. His vineyard is human nature. The laborers of the vineyard are all the saints who serve the salvation of human beings. The first hour is the time of those God-fearing men around Abel, Enoch, and Noah; for these were the first God-fearing men, the first laborers of the vineyard. Noah planted a vineyard—understand it spiritually, for these words are spiritual. They worked until the third hour. After the third hour comes the time of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; these too are laborers for our salvation, three in number, and for that reason they worked until the sixth hour. orientation: Cyril opens his homily by quoting the parable and then begins to decode each element: the landowner is God, the vineyard is human nature, and the hours are the ages of salvation history.
